title: The Israel–Iran conflict: So, now what?
excerpt: The June 2025 post on the conflict, U.S. involvement, and the questions that followed.
author: Shari Explains
coverAlt: Original cover artwork for The Israel–Iran conflict: So, now what?
body:
## So, now what?

On June 21st, 2025, the U.S. launched 3 nuclear strikes against the country of Iran. So, now what?

## Who’s involved in Iran conflict? United States

President Donald Trump: First U.S. president to attack another country’s nuclear program. Supported Israel’s military actions. Advocated for regime change in Tehran. Re-imposed sanctions and launched the ‘maximum pressure’ campaign. Ordered airstrikes (e.g., killing Qasem Soleimani in 2020). Supported direct negotiations with Iran after restoring sanctions.

U.S Forces: Operate across Middle Eastern bases (Qatar, Iraq, Syria). Responded to Iranian attacks and proxy activity with airstrikes.

## Israel

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: Advocated for strikes against Iran to halt its nuclear ambitions. Ordered the June 2024 airstrike targeting Iranian nuclear facilities.

Israeli Forces: Targeted Iranian nuclear sites and senior military leaders. Advocated for and implemented a pre-emptive military approach.

## Iran

Hassan Rouhani: Former president, elected 2013. Advocated for the JCPOA to lift sanctions and restore the economy.

Mohammad Bagheri: Iran’s military commander in chief (killed in Israel airstrikes). Second highest commander after the Supreme Leader.

Hossein Salami: Commander of the IRGC (Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps). Killed in Israel airstrikes.

Qasem Soleimani: Commander of the Quds Force (IRGC’s international arm). Killed by a U.S. airstrike in 2020.

Iranian Hardliners: Strengthened after the re-imposition of U.S. sanctions.

Iranian Nuclear Scientists & Senior Military Commanders: Targeted in Israel airstrikes and assassinations.

## Other forces involved

Houthi Rebels (Yemen): Supported by Iran. Engaged in attacks aligning with Iran-backed resistance.

Hezbollah (Lebanon): Iran-backed group, part of the ‘Axis of Resistance.’ Participated in direct attacks and proxy operations. Significantly weakened after Israeli decapitation strikes.

Quds Force (IRGC): Operated across Syria, Iraq, Lebanon, and Yemen. Trained and funded over 100,000 Shiite fighters across the Middle East.

Hamas: Targeted by Israel and weakened by the killing of its leaders. Part of Iran’s regional coalition.

## Other international players

P5+1 Coalition (USA, UK, France, Germany, Russia, and China): Negotiated the JCPOA agreement with Iran (2015). Played a role in international efforts to halt Iran’s nuclear program.

Saudi Arabia: Targeted by Iran-backed Houthis (oil facilities). Supported by the U.S. in bolstering air defenses.

## Timeline of events: Root cause

The Israeli government and the Iranian government have long been at odds with each other, with Iran supporting anti-Israeli militias, and Israel preventing Iran from building nuclear weapons.

## 2019–2020

2019: Israeli forces carried out a series of attacks against Iran’s allies (Syria, Lebanon, and Iraq) to prevent Iran from arming them with weapons. Israel accuses Iran of trying to establish a weapons supply in its allied countries to arm the Lebanese militia group, Hezbollah.

2020: Israeli forces killed Iran’s highest-ranked nuclear scientist, Moshen Fakhrizadeh, via a remote controlled machine gun.

## 2021–2023

2021: Iran and Israel started launching sea-based attacks at each other, with both Israel and Iran accusing each other of starting the attacks.

2022: Col. Sayad Khodayee, an officer in Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, was shot and killed by two assassins. Israeli officials claimed that Col. Khodayee helped command a covert operations unit that conducted assassinations and abductions.

2023: Palestinian militia group known as Hamas attacked Israel on Oct. 7th, while Hamas had spoken about receiving support from regional allies, Iran denied involvement in the attack.

## 2024–2025

2024: Anti-Israeli militia groups were being targeted and attacked in retaliation for the Oct 7th Attacks. Most notably, the leaders of both Hezbollah and Hamas were killed by Israeli forces.

2025: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu proposed to President Trump to bomb Iranian nuclear sites. Trump denied this proposal. Iran rejected the U.S.’s demand to stop all uranium enrichment.

## As of June 13th, 2025

On June 13th, 2025, Israel launched a major attack against Iran’s nuclear program. Iran launched retaliatory missile and drone strikes against Israel. The strikes between Israel and Iran have been some of the deadliest fighting in decades between the two countries. On Saturday, June 21st, 2025, fighting escalated when the U.S. bombed three Iranian nuclear sites.

## So… what now?

As of Tuesday, June 23rd, 2025, Iran and Israel have agreed to a ceasefire that President Trump claimed he orchestrated. A couple of hours before the ceasefire was supposed to go into effect, both Iran and Israel launched missiles at one another. One of these attacks killed, most notably, a high-profile nuclear scientist, Mohammad Reza Sedighi Saber, Iranian state TV reports.

If you are worried that Iran will bomb the U.S., they most likely won’t bomb us. The U.S. is a part of NATO. If Iran were to bomb the U.S., all NATO countries would have to retaliate. If a war were to break out between Israel and Iran, the U.S. would side with Israel for economic reasons, as Iran is rich in oil.

Democrats and (some) Republicans aren’t happy with the president. President Trump committed an act of war without getting approval from Congress beforehand, which isn’t allowed under Article 1 of the Constitution (as well as the War Powers Act of 1973). Trump’s act of war also directly goes against the U.N. Charter, which prohibits member countries from using excessive force, except in the case of self-defense. Senate minority (Democratic) leader Chuck Schumer is pushing for a vote so ‘all members of the Senate have to declare whether or not the US should be at war with Iran.’ A Kentucky congressman claimed that ‘Congress was on a vacation last week when all this was happening. We haven’t been briefed. They [the administration] should have called us all back.’
